auth.title: Long-Lived Access Tokens
highlights:
# Long-Lived Access Tokens

By default, Threads user access tokens are short-lived and are valid for one hour. However, short-lived tokens can be exchanged for long-lived tokens.

Long-lived tokens are valid for 60 days and can be refreshed as long as they are at least 24 hours old but have not expired, and the app user has granted your app the`threads_basic` permission. Refreshed tokens are valid for 60 days from the date at which they are refreshed. Tokens that have not been refreshed in 60 days will expire and can no longer be refreshed.

Long-lived access tokens for private Threads profiles can now be refreshed. In addition, permissions granted to apps by app users with private profiles are now valid for 90 days.

### Limitations

- Requests for long-lived tokens include your app secret so should only be made in server-side code, never in client-side code or in an app binary that could be decompiled. Do not share your app secret with anyone, expose it in code, send it to a client, or store it in a device.
- Expired short-lived tokens cannot be exchanged for long-lived tokens. If the user’s token has expired, get a new one before exchanging it for a long-lived token.

## Get a Long-Lived Token

Use the`GET /access_token` endpoint to exchange a short-lived Threads user access token for a long-lived token. Once you have a long-lived token, you can use it in server-side requests or send it to the client for use there.

Your request must be made server-side and include:

- Your Threads app secret (App Dashboard > App settings > Basic > Threads App secret).
- A valid (unexpired) short-lived Threads user access token.

### Parameters

Include the following query string parameters to augment the request.

`client_secret`

string

Required. Your Threads app's secret, displayed in the App Dashboard > App settings > Basic > Threads App secret field.

`grant_type`

string

Required. Set this to`th_exchange_token`.

`access_token`

string

Required. The valid (unexpired) short-lived Threads user access token that you want to exchange for a long-lived token.

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |

### Sample Request

```

curl -i -X GET "https://graph.threads.net/access_token
  ?grant_type=th_exchange_token
  &client_secret=<THREADS_APP_SECRET>
  &access_token=<SHORT_LIVED_ACCESS_TOKEN>"

```

### Sample Response

```

{
  "access_token": "<LONG_LIVED_USER_ACCESS_TOKEN>",
  "token_type": "bearer",
  "expires_in": 5183944  // number of seconds until token expires
}

```

## Refresh a Long-Lived Token

Use the`GET /refresh_access_token` endpoint to refresh unexpired long-lived Threads user access tokens. Refreshing a long-lived token makes it valid for 60 days again. Long-lived tokens that have not been refreshed in 60 days will expire.

Your request must include:

- A valid (unexpired) long-lived Threads user access token.

### Parameters

`grant_type`

string

Required. Set this to`th_refresh_token`.

`access_token`

string

Required. The valid (unexpired) long-lived Threads user access token that you want to refresh.

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |

### Sample Request

```

curl -i -X GET "https://graph.threads.net/refresh_access_token
  ?grant_type=th_refresh_token
  &access_token=<LONG_LIVED_ACCESS_TOKEN>"

```

### Sample Response

```

{
  "access_token": "<LONG_LIVED_USER_ACCESS_TOKEN>",
  "token_type": "bearer",
  "expires_in": 5183944 // number of seconds until token expires
}

```

auth.title: 入门指南
highlights:
# 入门指南

要访问 Threads API，请创建应用并挑选 Threads 用例。

本指南介绍快速入门 Threads API 所需的信息。

## 前期准备

您需要满足以下条件：

### Meta 应用

使用 Threads 用例 创建的 Meta 应用。

### 公共服务器

我们会下载您试图发布内容中所使用的影音内容，因此在试图发布之时，该影音内容必须托管在公共服务器上。

### 授权

数据访问授权由您的应用用户使用下列权限进行控制。用户必须通过授权窗口向您的应用授予这些权限，这样您的应用才可以访问用户数据。更多详情请参阅我们的 权限指南。

`threads_basic`：所有 Threads 端点的必需项。

`threads_content_publish`：Threads 发布端点的必需项。

`threads_manage_replies`：向回复端点发出`POST` 调用的必要条件。

`threads_read_replies`：向回复端点发出`GET` 调用的必要条件。

`threads_manage_insights`：向成效分析端点发出`GET` 调用的必要条件。

Threads 测试者可以在任何时候为您的应用授予这些权限。为了让在您的应用上没有身份的应用用户能够向该应用授予这些权限，每个权限都必须首先通过 应用审核 流程获得审批，并且您的应用必须已发布。

使用公共主页的应用用户的许可权限有效期为 90 天。如果授予口令的应用用户拥有公共主页，那么 刷新 应用用户的长期访问口令会将许可权限有效期再延长 90 天。如果应用用户的主页是 私密主页，则许可权限的有效期无法延长，应用用户必须在该权限过期后再次将其授予给您的应用。

### Threads 用户访问口令

API 身份验证由遵照 OAuth 2.0 协议的 Threads 用户访问口令处理。访问口令是应用范围口令（应用和用户对的独有口令），可以是短期或者长期口令。查询 Threads 用户或发布 Threads 影音内容的 API 请求必须包含 Threads 用户访问口令。使用 访问口令调试器 来调试 Threads 用户访问口令。

#### 短期访问口令

短期访问口令的有效期为 1 小时，但可以交换为 长期口令。如要获取短期访问口令，请将授权窗口部署到应用中。应用用户通过窗口验证其身份信息后，我们会将用户重定向回您的应用，并附上授权码，然后您可以用该授权码 交换短期访问口令。

#### 长期访问口令

尚未过期的短期口令可以 交换为长期访问口令（有效期为 60 天）。在长期口令失效前 刷新 口令的方法是查询`GET /refresh_access_token` 端点。

### 授权窗口

借助授权窗口，您的应用可以获取应用用户的授权码和权限。授权码可以交换为 Threads 用户访问口令，在获取应用用户的主页、检索 Threads 影音内容、发布帖子、阅读回复、管理回复或查看成效分析时必须包含这些口令。

如要部署授权窗口，请参阅 获取访问口令 指南。

### 授权码

授权码可用于交换短期 Threads 用户访问口令。如要获取授权码，请将授权窗口部署到应用中。应用用户在通过窗口验证其身份信息并授予应用所需的所有权限后，我们会将用户重定向至您的应用，并附上授权码。然后，您可以使用 API 将代码交换为应用用户的短期 Threads 用户访问口令。

注意：授权码是短期口令，有效期仅为 1 小时。

### Threads 测试者

要用 Threads 用户测试您的应用，您必须先向 Threads 用户的主页发送邀请并接受邀请。点击添加用户按钮，然后在应用面板 > 应用身份 > 身份选项卡中选择 Threads 测试者。

Threads 用户可以在登录账户后在 Threads 网站或移动版应用的 账户设置 下的网站权限版块接受邀请。

auth.title: Retrieve User Posts
highlights:
## Retrieve a List of All a User's Threads

Use the`GET /{threads-user-id}/threads` endpoint to return a paginated list of all threads created by a user.

### Permissions

The Threads Retrieval API requires an appropriate access token and permissions based on the node you are targeting. While you are testing, you can easily generate tokens and grant your app permissions by using the Graph API Explorer.

- `threads_basic`— Required for making any calls to all Threads API endpoints.

### Limitations

- You may only fetch a paginated list of all threads created by the app-scoped user.

...

### Example Request

```

curl -s -X GET \
"https://graph.threads.net/v1.0/me/threads?fields=id,media_product_type,media_type,media_url,permalink,owner,username,text,timestamp,shortcode,thumbnail_url,children,is_quote_post&since=2023-10-15&until=2023-11-18&limit=1&access_token=$THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN"

```

...

## Retrieve a Single Threads Media Object

You can also use the`GET /{threads-media-id}` endpoint to return an individual Threads media object.

### Permissions

The Threads Retrieval API requires an appropriate access token and permissions based on the node you are targeting. While you are testing, you can easily generate tokens and grant your app permissions by using the Graph API Explorer.

- `threads_basic`— Required for making any calls to all Threads API endpoints.

If your app has not been approved for advanced access for the`threads_basic` permission, only posts created by a Threads tester are retrievable. After approval, public posts created by other users will be retrievable.

### Example Request

```

curl -s -X GET \
"https://graph.threads.net/v1.0/<THREADS_MEDIA_ID>?fields=id,media_product_type,media_type,media_url,permalink,owner,username,text,timestamp,shortcode,thumbnail_url,children,is_quote_post&access_token=<THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN>"

```

gate.title: Overview - Threads API - Documentation - Meta for Developers
highlights:
# Overview

You may use the Threads API to enable people to create and publish content on a person’s behalf on Threads, and to display those posts within your app solely to the person who created it.

## Rate Limiting

Calls to the Threads API are counted against the calling app's call count. An app's call count is unique for each app and app user pair and is the number of calls the app has made in a rolling 24-hour window. It is calculated as follows:

`Calls within 24 hours = 4800 * Number of Impressions`

The Number of Impressions is the number of times any content from the app user's Threads account has entered a person's screen within the last 24 hours. Rate limiting may also be subject to total CPU time per day:

`720000 * number_of_impressions for total_cputime 
      2880000 * Number of Impressions for total_time`

Note: The minimum value for impressions is 10 (so if the impressions is less than 10 we default to 10).

### Posts

Threads profiles are limited to 250 API-published posts within a 24-hour moving period. Carousels count as a single post. This limit is enforced on the`POST /{threads-user-id}/threads_publish` endpoint when attempting to publish a media container. We recommend that your app also enforces the publishing rate limit, especially if your app allows app users to schedule posts to be published in the future.

To check a profile's current Threads API rate limit usage, query the GET /{threads-user-id}/threads_publishing_limit endpoint.

Note: This endpoint requires the`threads_basic` and`threads_content_publish` permissions.

...

`quota_usage`

Threads publishing count over the last 24 hours.

...

Threads publishing rate limit config object, which contains the`quota_total` and`quota_duration` fields.

gate.title: Threads API Pricing 2026: Free, but Rate-Limited
highlights:
- URL: https://www.blotato.com/blog/threads-api-pricing
- Published: 2026-07-01 (updated 2026-11-20)
- Author: Sabrina Ramonov, Founder, Blotato
- Category: Developer Guide

---

Threads API pricing in 2026 is free. Meta publishes no paid tier, no per-call fee, and no pricing page in the official Threads developer docs.

...

There is no dollar cost, but "free" hides two ceilings you plan around instead of a price.

...

## Threads API Pricing at a Glance (2026)

| Access path | Cost | Best for | Key friction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Threads API (Meta, official) | No paid tier or per-call fee published | Posting, replying, reading insights on your own account | Meta App Review for non-tester users, 60-day long-lived tokens, 500-char text cap |
| Threads Tester access | No paid tier or per-call fee published | Prototyping before app review | Each tester must accept an invite, app stays in development mode |
| RapidAPI Meta Threads wrapper | Vendor-listed plans starting at $0/month (verify on the vendor page before subscribing) | Read-only scraping at low volume | Unofficial, no SLA, scraping ToS risk |
| EnsembleData Threads endpoints | Vendor-listed plans from a $0 free tier (50 units/day) up to about $1,400/month, with a custom Diamond tier above | Bulk public-data extraction | Read-only, no posting capability |
| Data365 Threads scraper | Basic €300/mo, Standard €850/mo, Custom tier, 14-day no-card free trial, not affiliated with Meta | Public-data scraping at one or more platforms | Vendor explicitly disclaims Meta partnership |
| Blotato unified API | Starter $29/mo, Creator $97/mo, Agency $499/mo | Posting Threads + 10 other platforms from one endpoint | API access on paid plans only, generating a key ends the free trial |

The honest answer is that Meta has not published a paid tier or per-call fee for the Threads API, which is what most readers mean by "free." The catch is that production access is still gated by Meta App Review and capped by a rate-limit formula tied to your account's impression volume, which we walk through below.

For teams that just need to publish to Threads (and ten other platforms) without writing the OAuth flow themselves, Blotato wires the whole posting layer up behind one endpoint and removes the app-review step from the critical path. The dashboard has a 7-day free trial. The Blotato API runs on paid plans starting at $29/month.

A Threads post through Blotato takes one media item, and the workaround for more is a thread.

Dashboard trial: 7 days · API access: paid plans only

...

### Official Threads API (no published paid tier)

The official Threads API surface lives entirely inside the Meta for Developers portal and has no published paid tier. You create a Meta app, add the Threads use case, request the permissions you need, and go through Meta App Review to take your app out of development mode.

The core scopes on Meta's overview and get-started pages are `threads_basic`, `threads_content_publish`, `threads_read_replies`, `threads_manage_replies`, `threads_manage_insights`, `threads_delete`, and `threads_location_tagging`. Three more live on dedicated sub-pages: `threads_keyword_search`, `threads_manage_mentions`, and `threads_profile_discovery`. A newer `threads_share_to_instagram` scope was added on March 25, 2026, authorizing the `crossreshare_to_ig` and `crossreshare_to_ig_dark_mode` parameters on the publishing endpoint. Pull from whichever sub-page matches your use case.

Once your app is approved, it can act on any user who completes the OAuth flow, subject to the rate-limit formula below and the 24-hour caps. Meta's public Threads API docs do not list a monthly subscription, a per-call charge, or a paid quota-increase product anywhere on the developer surface.

...

### Threads Tester access (no review needed)

Before app review, your app stays in development mode. You invite Threads Testers, and each gets the permissions you've configured immediately after accepting the invite (Meta caps the tester count per app at the platform-wide limit, so check the current ceiling on your app's roles page). This is the path indie developers use to ship for themselves: invite yourself as a tester, build the integration, skip app review as long as the only users are accepted testers.

The catch is the app stays private. You cannot onboard arbitrary users until the app is approved through review.

...

## The Real Cost: Meta App Review and Token Refresh

Meta does not publish a paid tier or per-call fee for the Threads API, but production access is not free of calendar time or maintenance. The cost shows up in two places.

App review. To use the Threads API for any non-Tester user, you submit each permission for Meta App Review with a screencast, privacy policy, terms-of-service URL, and (for many permissions) business verification. First-round rejections are common. Meta's App Review introduction says processing "typically takes less than one week, often only 2 to 3 days," with longer windows during high volume.

Token refresh. Short-lived tokens last 1 hour. Long-lived tokens last 60 days and refresh between 24 hours and 60 days from issue (the token must still carry `threads_basic`). Permissions from users on private profiles expire after 90 days. Build a refresh job before the 60-day mark plus a re-permission flow for private-profile users.

Neither is a dollar cost. Both are calendar costs. They are the reason indie builders who only need to post to their own account often skip app review and stay in development mode with accepted testers.

# Register as a Meta Developer

This document explains how to register as a Meta developer. Once you have registered you will have access to the App Dashboard and all of our products, SDKs, APIs, development tools, and developer documentation.

## Step 1: Start the registration process

While logged into your Facebook account, go to https://developers.facebook.com/async/registration.

Alternatively, you can go to the Social Technologies Dev Center website and click Get Started.

## Step 2: Agree to our Terms and Policies

Click Next to agree to our Platform Terms and Developer Policies.

## Step 3: Verify your account

We will send a confirmation code to the phone number and email address that you provide in order to confirm that you have access to them. Your number and email will be used for important developer notifications of any changes that may impact to your app.

## Step 4: Select your occupation

Select an occupation that most closely describes what you do for a living.

## Next Steps

Now that you have registered you can use the App Dashboard to create your first app.

highlights:
A Threads MCP server gives an AI agent tools for Threads, so a model can publish to your account instead of only drafting posts. Point Claude, Cursor, or any MCP client at Outstand's server and the agent can post text with optional media, chain a multi-post thread, repost, quote, reply to comments, and read views and engagement. Everything goes through Meta's official Threads API over an OAuth connection you approve once.

...

## Does Threads have an official MCP server?

No. Meta does not publish an MCP server for Threads.

Threads is also the thinnest ecosystem of any major network here. Where Instagram and X have dozens of community servers of varying quality, Threads has very few, and most of what exists is experimental. That cuts both ways: there is less to evaluate, and less risk of installing something abandoned, but there is also almost nothing to fall back on.

Outstand's is a hosted server on Meta's official Threads API. You connect with a normal OAuth consent screen, the server calls the documented publishing endpoints, and Threads gets the same tool surface as every other network you post to. If you are building agent workflows on Threads now, being early is most of the point.

# meta-threads-mcp

Unofficial MCP server for Meta's Threads API. Enables LLMs like Claude to publish posts, manage replies, and track insights through the Model Context Protocol.

[!PyPI version](https://pypi.org/project/meta-threads-mcp/)
[!Python 3.12+](https://www.python.org/downloads/)
[!License: MIT](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)

## Features

- Full Threads API coverage via MCP tools
- Create text, image, and video posts
- Reply management (reply, hide/unhide, get conversation)
- Post and user insights/metrics
- Publishing quota tracking
- Built on meta-threads-sdk and FastMCP

...

## Available Tools

### Posts

| Tool | Description | Parameters |
|------|-------------|------------|
| `threads_create_post` | Create and publish a text post | `text` (required), `reply_control` (optional) |
| `threads_create_image_post` | Create post with image | `image_url` (required), `text` (optional) |
| `threads_create_video_post` | Create post with video | `video_url` (required), `text` (optional) |
| `threads_get_post` | Get a post by ID | `post_id` (required) |
| `threads_get_user_posts` | Get user's recent posts | `limit` (optional, default 10) |
| `threads_delete_post` | Delete a post | `post_id` (required) |
| `threads_get_publishing_limit` | Check remaining quota | none |

### Replies

| Tool | Description | Parameters |
|------|-------------|------------|
| `threads_reply_to_post` | Reply to a post | `post_id` (required), `text` (required) |

mcp.title: baguskto/threads-mcp
highlights:
# Threads MCP Server

An MCP server for the **official Meta Threads API**. Let Claude (or any MCP client) publish posts, carousels, polls, replies and quotes, read your posts, replies, mentions and insights, search public posts, and schedule posts — using only endpoints Meta documents.

- Built on the MCP TypeScript SDK v2 (`@modelcontextprotocol/server`), works with clients on protocol 2024-11-05 through 2025-11-25
- 42 tools, each annotated as read-only or write so clients can auto-approve reads and confirm writes
- Waits for media processing before publishing, retries transient errors, and validates posts before anything goes live
- Optional read-only mode, and no token required just to start the server and list tools

> **v6 is a rewrite.** Tools that called endpoints the Threads API does not have (likes, follows, blocks, follower lists, trending) were removed, and several were renamed or merged. See Migrating from v5.

## Quick start

### 1. Get an access token

1. Create an app at developers.facebook.com and add the **Threads API** use case.
2. Add yourself as a Threads tester and accept the invite in Threads (Settings → Account → Website permissions).
3. Request the scopes you need (see Permissions); `threads_basic` and `threads_content_publish` cover posting.
4. Generate a user token, then turn it into a **long-lived token** (60 days). You can do the exchange from the server with `exchange_for_long_lived_token` if you set `THREADS_APP_SECRET`.

A Threads profile no longer needs a linked Instagram account, except for follower counts and demographics.

### 2. Add the server to your client

**Claude Code**

```bash
claude mcp add threads --env THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN=your_token -- npx -y threads-mcp-server
```

**Claude Desktop** (`claude_desktop_config.json`) and other clients that use the same format:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "threads": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "threads-mcp-server"],
      "env": {
        "THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN": "your_long_lived_token"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Requires Node.js 20 or newer.

### 3. Check the setup

Ask the assistant to run `validate_setup`. It confirms the token works, shows when it expires, and lists missing scopes together with the tools they unlock.

## Configuration

| Variable | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN` | yes | Long-lived Threads user token |
| `THREADS_USER_ID` | no | Your Threads user ID; skips one `/me` lookup |
| `THREADS_APP_SECRET` | no | Enables `exchange_for_long_lived_token` |
| `THREADS_READ_ONLY` | no | `true` to expose only read tools (no publishing, deleting or scheduling) |
| `THREADS_PUBLISH_WAIT_SECONDS` | no | How long a publish call waits for media processing before returning the pending container (default 45) |
| `THREADS_SCHEDULE_FILE` | no | Where scheduled posts are stored (default `~/.threads-mcp/scheduled-posts.json`). Keep it on a local disk, not a network or synced folder |
| `THREADS_API_VERSION` | no | Graph API version (default `v1.0`) |
| `THREADS_API_BASE_URL` | no | Graph host (default `https://graph.threads.net`; must be HTTPS) |

Configuration is read only from the environment your MCP client passes in. A `.env` file in the working directory is intentionally ignored, because clients often launch servers inside projects you may not trust.

...

### Publishing

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `publish_thread` | Text, image or video post. Text posts can add a link preview, a poll (2–4 options), a GIPHY GIF, a long-form text attachment (up to 10,000 characters) or be a 24-hour ghost post. Every post can set spoiler ranges, a topic tag, reply control, location, country allowlist, reply approvals and Instagram Story cross-sharing. `publish: false` creates a draft container instead. |
| `create_carousel_post` | 2–20 images and/or videos with alt text |
| `create_reply` | Reply to a post, with the same options as `publish_thread` |
| `quote_post` | Quote another post |
| `create_thread_chain` | Multi-part thread; every part is validated before the first one goes live, and a failure tells you where to resume |
| `repost_thread` | Repost a post |
| `delete_thread` | Delete one of your posts |
| `get_container_status` / `publish_container` | Inspect and publish a container later (drafts, or slow videos) |

Video and image processing can take a while. Each publish call waits up to 45 seconds in total (so it finishes before typical MCP client timeouts) and sends progress notifications while it waits. If media is still processing after that, it returns the pending `container_id` instead of failing, and `publish_container` finishes the job; a thread chain returns the parts it published and where to resume. Cancelling a request stops it before anything further is published.

### Scheduling

The Threads API has no native scheduling, so `schedule_post` saves the post locally and this server publishes it at the requested time. The server has to be running then; anything overdue is published as soon as it starts. Media containers are created at publish time, since they expire after 24 hours.

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `schedule_post` | Schedule a post, reply, quote or carousel for an ISO 8601 time |
| `list_scheduled_posts` | Pending, published, failed and cancelled posts with their results |
| `cancel_scheduled_post` | Cancel a pending post |

### Reading

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `get_my_threads` | Your posts, with date filters |
| `get_thread` | One post by ID |
| `search_my_threads` | Find text in your own posts |
| `get_mentions` | Public posts that mention you |
| `get_ghost_posts` | Your ghost posts |
| `get_poll_results` | Options, vote percentages and expiry of a poll |
| `lookup_profile` / `get_profile_posts` | Public profiles and their posts, by username |
| `get_oembed` | Embed HTML for a post |
| `create_web_intent_link` | A threads.com link that opens a prefilled composer or a follow prompt — for things the API can't do, like following |

### Replies

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `get_thread_replies` | Top-level replies to a post |
| `get_conversation` | The whole conversation, flattened |
| `get_my_replies` | Replies you posted |
| `manage_reply` | Hide or unhide a reply |
| `get_pending_replies` / `manage_pending_reply` | Review replies on posts published with reply approvals |

### Insights

| Tool | What it does |

...

| `get_thread_insights` | Views, likes, replies, reposts, quotes and shares for a post |
| `get_my_insights` | Account views (per day), likes, replies, reposts, quotes, link clicks and follower count |
| `get_audience_demographics` | Followers by country, city, age or gender (100+ followers) |
| `get_content_performance_report` | Totals, averages, engagement rate, results by media type and top posts over a window, from real per-post insights |
| `analyze_best_posting_times` | Weekdays and hours when your own posts performed best, in your timezone |

...

| Tool | What it does |

...

| `search_posts` | Keyword or topic-tag search, TOP or RECENT, filtered by media type, author and date |
| `get_recently_searched_keywords` | Your recent searches |
| `search_locations` /

...

## Permissions

| Scope | Unlocks |
| --- | --- |
| `threads_basic` | Every tool |
| `threads_content_publish` | Posts, carousels, quotes, reposts, thread chains |
| `threads_manage_replies` | Publishing replies, hiding replies, reply approvals |
| `threads_read_replies` | Reading replies and conversations |
| `threads_manage_insights` | Insights, demographics, reports |
| `threads_manage_mentions` | Mentions |
| `threads_keyword_search` | Searching beyond your own posts |
| `threads_delete` | Deleting posts |
| `threads_location_tagging` | Location search and tagging |
| `threads_profile_discovery` | Public profile lookup |
| `threads_share_to_instagram` | Cross-sharing to Instagram Stories |

Until Meta approves an advanced permission, some tools only see your own or your testers' data — for example, search returns only your posts and profile lookup works only for official Meta accounts.

## What the Threads API can't do

There are no endpoints for liking, following, blocking, listing followers, listing likers, trending feeds, direct messages, editing posts, uploading files (media must be public URLs) or undoing a repost. This server doesn't pretend otherwise. For following, `create_web_intent_link` gives you a link to click.

mcp.title: Threads MCP Server for Claude and ChatGPT | Spreadcast
highlights:
## What a Threads MCP Server Is

A Threads MCP server is a small program that lets an AI assistant post to Threads for you. Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code or Cursor never talk to Threads directly. They talk to the server through the Model Context Protocol, which the official MCP introduction calls an open source standard for connecting AI applications to outside systems, and compares to a USB C port for AI apps. The server then calls Meta's Threads API: it makes a post, attaches a picture, publishes a carousel, reads replies or pulls the numbers on last week's posts.

...

## Is There an Official Meta Threads MCP Server?

No. On October 28, 2026 Meta runs one MCP server, and it is for ads. Meta's Ads MCP server overview describes a server hosted at mcp.facebook.com/ads with seven groups of tools: reporting, ad creation and management, catalogs, signals and datasets, help and troubleshooting, A/B tests and lift studies, and activity logs. It does not mention Threads, and it does not publish organic posts anywhere.

We found no Meta page, developer blog post or GitHub repository from Meta that describes a Threads MCP server. So when people search for a Meta Threads MCP, what they find is one of two things: a community server that calls Meta's official Threads API with a token you create, or a hosted service that has its own approved Meta app and lets you sign in. Both are legitimate. Neither is Meta's.

What Meta does publish is the API itself and a reference app. The Threads API launch post, dated June 18, 2024, says the API is open to all developers and lists publishing, fetching your own posts, reply management and insights. Meta also keeps an open source sample app on GitHub that shows the sign in and publishing calls. Every honest Threads MCP server is a wrapper around those same calls, which is why the limits in the next sections apply to all of them.

...

## What the Threads API Lets Any MCP Server Do

The Threads API is what decides what a Threads MCP server can and cannot do. A server can be clever about how it calls the API, but it cannot add a feature Meta does not offer. Anthropic introduced MCP on November 25, 2024, five months after the Threads API opened, and every Threads server since has been built on top of that June 2024 API.

Publishing works in two calls. Meta's publishing guide says you first create a media container with the text and any picture or video, then publish that container. For a carousel you make one container per item, flagged as a carousel item, then a carousel container that lists them, then publish. Meta recommends waiting about 30 seconds on average before publishing a container, so the picture or video has time to process. Media is not uploaded as a file: Threads fetches it from a link, and the get started guide says that link must be on a publicly reachable server at the moment of the attempt.

Beyond plain posts, the API supports a few Threads specific extras. A text post can carry a link preview through a link attachment field. A post can carry one topic tag of 1 to 50 characters, without periods or ampersands. A text post can attach a GIF, with GIPHY as the only provider. Polls, spoilers, text attachments, quote posts and reposts each have their own reference pages. The API also lets you read your own posts, read and hide replies, reply as yourself and pull insights.

Insights deserve a line of their own, because many people want an assistant to report on Threads. Meta's insights reference lists views, likes, replies, reposts, quotes and shares per post, and views, likes, replies, reposts, quotes, link clicks, follower count and follower demographics per profile. Two catches: reading insights needs its own permission, and follower demographics need a profile with at least 100 followers.

What the API does not have matters as much. There is no scheduling: you cannot hand Threads a post and a future time. Any server that schedules keeps the post itself and publishes it when the time comes. There is no endpoint to like posts, follow people or read someone's follower list.

mcp.title: NabuxAi/threads-mcp
highlights:
by Nabux

Multi-user, multi-account MCP gateway powered by Meta's official ... API.

- Production target: `https://threads.nabuxai.com
...
- MCP: `https://threads.nabuxai.com/mcp`
- OAuth callback: `https://threads.nabuxai.com/threads/callback`

##

> Remote MCP server (streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1) that gives an AI agent access to one user's Threads (threads.com) account: publishing, replies and moderation, search and insights.

MCP endpoint: https://threads-mcp.app/mcp

## When to use this

Use Threads for Claude when the user wants to act on **their own Threads account** from a chat:

- Publish to Threads: a single text/image/video post, a carousel of 2–20 items, or a multi-part thread from long-form text.
- Manage conversations: read replies and mentions, reply, hide spam replies, repost, delete their posts.
- Write better posts: check a draft before publishing (hidden characters, stock AI phrases, Threads limits) and get a cleaned version.
- Learn what works: audit the user's own posts by engagement rate, reply ratio and reach, with sample sizes.
- Report on performance: views, likes, replies, reposts, quotes and shares per post or for a date range ("what performed best this month?"), and account-level metrics and follower demographics.
- Research: search public Threads posts by keyword or topic tag, look up public profiles and their recent posts.

Do not use it for:

- Instagram, Facebook or X/Twitter; it only covers Threads.
- Scheduling posts for later: Threads has no scheduling API, so publish when the user approves.
- Reading likes or views of other people's posts; Threads only exposes metrics for the user's own posts.
- Anonymous or unattended use; every call runs as a signed-in Threads user who connected the account.
